crime_highlights: the attack was done by four persons on one victim who was essentially defenceless given the four-on-one scenario
there was the protracted nature of the attack and the beating
the parties stopped and obtained bear mace
they broke down the hotel door, dragged Willcocks out of bed and out of the hotel to the waiting van, and gratuitously beat up the roommate who was present in the hotel room at the time
rationale_highlights: the aboriginal backgrounds of these four accused still must be considered in fixing fit and proper sentences for each of them

the mitigating factors which, to some extent, must be taken into account being the fact that there were guilty pleas to manslaughter by all four accused at the earliest possible time, coupled with their aboriginal heritage
their developmental history appears to some extent in each case to have been affected by their upbringing
note: Crime narrative para 7 too long; used court's summary. Effect stated only generally.

crime_highlights: Toby Daniel Baptiste is before me for sentencing following upon his conviction on a single count of breaking and entering a dwelling place
Mr. Baptiste, in a state of insobriety, entered into the residence of a resident on the Sunshine Coast near Sechelt, British Columbia, uninvited
his lengthy record, which, depending on how one counts and what one counts, portrays either 12 or 17 offences of a similar kind in the period between 1994 and this conviction
rationale_highlights: there is undoubtedly some substance to the claim in this case for the reason that the indications are that Mr. Baptiste's father was a resident at a residential school
I am required and indeed think it appropriate to consider the direction in 718.2, which is that I take into account Mr. Baptiste's circumstances as a member of the aboriginal community
I am not persuaded that a period of incarceration absent a conditional sentence is appropriate
note: Court never states clearly that the factor reduced the sentence.

crime_highlights: Of the three, this offender was the most highly intoxicated
The offender did not hold a British Columbia driver's licence
The offender was driving his motor vehicle; the two other young people were occupants

It left the travelled surface of the roadway at not less than 70 kilometres per hour, which was an excessive speed in the circumstances, and collided with a utility pole, severing that pole horizontally
In the result, the other two young people, the occupants, were fatally injured.
rationale_highlights: As further material for my performing my duty under the Gladue principles

I see nothing in any of the material I have read from his background or his aboriginal heritage that would explain why a disposition involving him should be any different than any other drunken driver
He is of an aboriginal background.
note: Court finds Gladue background does not explain offence or change disposition.
